solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish American lawyer caught — and ate, ultimately

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word ate

explanation.surface: A fish is snatched up and eaten by an American attorney, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes only the E at the end of 'ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dace is a small freshwater fish of the carp family, an example of the class.

clue.text: Dire sort said to flourish over America

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting over another comes first
to flourish is to wave about with a flamboyant gesture, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: A grim sort of person is said to prosper on top of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flourish' is the anagram signal for SORT SAID. 'said' looks like a sound signal but is only fodder, and 'over' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a situation that is calamitous or catastrophically bad; they are synonyms.

clue.text: People pursuing further drinks

definitions.meaning: those who run after someone or something
drinks taken after another, such as a beer after a whisky shot

explanation.surface: Revellers go after another round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuers chase; a drink downed straight after a stronger one is a follow-up of the same name.

clue.text: Linesman's acknowledgement of clever remark about days in jail

indicators.note: about means going round, so the acknowledgement wraps the rest

parts.note: touché is said to admit that someone has scored a witty point

indicators.note: in means the days abbreviation is placed within the jail word

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: An official recognises a witty remark about a few days spent behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'about' nest the pieces, giving JUDG within the acknowledgement. A touch judge is the rugby union linesman, so 'Linesman' is not a railway worker.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the official running the sideline flags is called a touch judge; it is the sport's term for an assistant referee.

clue.text: Accidentally picked up report of animal minder's position

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the following phrase is to be said out loud

parts.note: a herdsman stands watch over the herd

explanation.surface: Someone happened to hear a story about where a farmhand stands.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal minder is above his flock: 'over herd', which sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear something by chance, not meant for your ears, is the sense of eavesdropping unintentionally.

clue.text: Bill's companion catches cold, needing a warm drink

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so the companion word takes in the cold letter

parts.note: the phrase bill and coo pairs the word with bill, as lovebirds do
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Bill's partner catches a chill and needs something hot to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but belongs to the phrase 'bill and coo'. 'catches' puts C inside COO, giving COCO, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate-flavoured beverage made from powdered cacao beans is a classic warm bedtime drink.

clue.text: Defence originally advanced in only one literary genre

parts.note: just means merely or only
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in means the opening letter sits within the genre word

parts.note: fiction is the genre of invented prose stories

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A defence was first put forward in a single type of novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes A from 'advanced', and 'in' puts it inside FICTION to give FICATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A justification is a reason offered in defence of an action, the grounds for excusing it.

clue.text: Addict finally consumed most of 3's game, I gathered

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word consumed
gathered means taken in, so the shortened game word collects the I
most of means the last letter is dropped from the game word

parts.note: entry 3, the touch judge, officiates at rugby, known informally as rugger

explanation.surface: A user who has finally overdosed is gathered up during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives D from 'consumed'. 'most of' cuts RUGGER, the British slang for rugby union, to RUGGE, and 'gathered' puts I inside it to give RUGGIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Druggie is informal slang for a habitual drug user, someone hooked on narcotics.

clue.text: English cleric's flat

parts.note: Ven., short for Venerable, is the title of an Anglican archdeacon

explanation.surface: An English clergyman's apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a noun for a home, but it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A level surface with no bumps is smooth and flat; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Consequence of situation surrounding ancient city

indicators.note: surrounding means the situation word goes round the city

parts.note: a state is a condition or situation
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: The outcome of circumstances around an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consequence' here means importance, as in a person of consequence, not a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing or importance in the eyes of others, as when a figure gains stature in public life.

clue.text: Like gripping book lacking capacity to include crushing remark

indicators.note: to include means the first word holds the remark inside it

parts.note: unable means without the capacity to do something
a put-down is a humiliating comment

explanation.surface: A thrilling novel apparently can't hold a cutting insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' signals insertion; the remark splits the outer word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A book so engrossing you cannot stop reading it is described with this informal adjective.

clue.text: Price university may exact at first for clothing

parts.note: cost means price

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of may and exact

explanation.surface: A university may charge a price for clothing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes M and E from 'may' and 'exact'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit worn for a play or a fancy-dress party is a set of clothes, a kind of garb.

clue.text: Two women by an enclosure holding record for farm activity

indicators.note: holding means the pair of pronouns keep the record between them
Two means the pronoun for a woman is written twice

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
EP is an extended-play record
a ring is an enclosed area, as in a boxing ring or bullring

explanation.surface: Two women next to a pen with a record playing, out on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles the pronoun, and 'holding' places the record between the two copies rather than around both.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping the fleece off the flock is a seasonal job done by farmers, an example of farm work.

clue.text: Feat involving Tim and Netta, not daughter

indicators.note: involving suggests the names are mixed together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A daring stunt performed by a couple called Tim and Netta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not daughter' removes D from TIM AND NETTA, and 'involving' rearranges the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement or accomplishment, something successfully reached, is a feat by another name.

clue.text: Meet at end of scripture exam — again

indicators.note: at end of means the meeting word comes after the scripture abbreviation

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject of scripture
a court or committee sits when it meets in session

explanation.surface: A gathering at the close of a scripture test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exam — again' is a definition read as 'an exam taken again'. RE (religious education) is the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A second attempt at a failed test is a repeat examination.

clue.text: Wren eg, male, grabbing insect's tail, caught on outside

indicators.note: on outside places the cricket abbreviation on the end, after the rest
grabbing means the name holds the letter within

parts.note: Archie is a man's name

indicators.note: tail points to the final letter of the word insect

parts.note: CT is a cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A wren, say, a male bird, seizing an insect's tail and caught out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' is Sir Christopher Wren, designer of St Paul's Cathedral, not the bird. 'tail' takes T from 'insect's', and 'grabbing' puts it in ARCHIE to give ARCHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren designed buildings, so he is an example of a professional designer of buildings.

clue.text: Inhibit firm led by right-wing politician

indicators.note: led by means the politician comes first in this down entry

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative
strict means firm or rigorous

explanation.surface: A conservative leader holds back a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective meaning strict.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict or limit, holding something back, is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Description of virgin territory don turned out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic was sent away from unexplored land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DON TURNED; 'turned' looks like a reversal sign but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Land where nobody has yet walked is never stepped on, so the adjective describes virgin ground.

clue.text: Racecourse character's quiet way to stop row

indicators.note: to stop means plug a gap, so the pieces sit inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A racegoer's quiet method of ending a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as an argument but is a line of seats, TIER, with P and ST placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person at the races who sells predictions of winners is a familiar track figure.

clue.text: Hunting cry from Cockney in Scottish town

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: halloa is a shout urging on hounds

explanation.surface: A huntsman's shout is heard from a Londoner in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in Clackmannanshire, central Scotland, on the River Forth.

clue.text: Largely similar to a ballet, oddly attractive

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: like means similar to

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of ballet

explanation.surface: Something rather like a strange ballet is appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' cuts LIKE to LIK, and 'oddly' takes B, L, E from 'ballet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and easy to be fond of, as a charming person is; a synonym.

clue.text: Terrified old nurse stabbed by kid on grass

indicators.note: on means the stabbed nurse follows the grass

parts.note: panic is a type of grass, panic grass

indicators.note: stabbed by means the hoax word is pushed into the nurse

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
to kid is to fool, and a trick is a hoax

explanation.surface: A former nurse is knifed by a youngster on a lawn, leaving her terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but means a trick. SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing grade now discontinued.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcome by sudden alarm is the sense of being scared out of one's wits.

clue.text: My fine, initially unspoiled, holiday destination?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of unspoiled

explanation.surface: Wow, a lovely untouched spot for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, COR, a British expression of surprise. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek island in the Ionian Sea that is a popular resort, an example of a getaway spot.

clue.text: Business enterprise completed takeover

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A firm finalises its acquisition of a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takeover' is the seizing of power by force, as in a military coup.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden seizure of government power, as by the army, is a kind of takeover.

clue.text: Month in which men will secure court award

indicators.note: will secure means the men hold the following pieces between them

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A month when the workforce will be given a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the calendar year is one of the twelve months.

clue.text: Old coin found by soldier going over base

indicators.note: going over means turning the soldier abbreviation backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: An old coin is discovered by a soldier passing over a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking honour, mean-spirited and dishonourable conduct is described by both words.

clue.text: Maintain head has adopted favoured uniform with hesitation

indicators.note: has adopted means the head takes the other pieces into it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
er is the sound of hesitation
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A headteacher keeps things going by adopting a preferred school uniform, hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has adopted' puts the three inserted pieces after the head's first letter; the hesitation comes first in the answer although the clue names it last.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going indefinitely is to preserve or continue it, a synonym.

clue.text: Inclination to be crooked

definitions.meaning: a natural tendency or aptitude for something
dishonest or corrupt, or literally not straight

explanation.surface: A tendency to be dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning or talent is a flair; a dishonest copper is called curved, out of straight.
